title: Snell's Law — Light Bends at the Boundary
learning_objectives: State n₁ sin θ₁ = n₂ sin θ₂
Predict bend toward/away from the normal
Recognize total internal reflection past the critical angle
voiceover: Light travels in straight lines — until it meets a new medium.
At the air–water boundary, part of the ray reflects, and part refracts.
Snell's Law says n-one sine theta-one equals n-two sine theta-two.
From air into water, the ray bends toward the normal.
From water into air, beyond the critical angle, the ray reflects totally — fiber optics use this.
